Reports indicate that Apple has significantly increased its orders for vapor chambers, suggesting that this cooling technology is expected to play a more important role in its future hardware product line. Details are as follows.

Apple Increases Bet on Vapor Chamber Cooling Technology

Leaker Fixed Focus Digital posted on Weibo stating that Apple has "significantly increased its total vapor chamber orders," and said the move "may be in preparation for enhanced cooling for the first foldable iPhone and the next-generation 20th anniversary model."

Apple first introduced vapor chamber cooling technology in the iPhone 17 Pro, a change that helped address thermal issues that had plagued previous models.

The operating principle of a vapor chamber involves evaporating a small amount of liquid near a heat source, then condensing it in a cooler area to disperse the heat across a larger surface, before allowing the liquid to flow back and repeat the cycle.

You can learn how it actually works through this excellent video from Know Art below:

Although the Weibo post speculated that Apple's increased orders are aimed at the iPhone Ultra and the 20th anniversary iPhone expected to launch in 2027, based on timing, it seems more likely that this year's product lineup will adopt the technology.

Apple is reportedly asking suppliers to prepare approximately 10 million foldable iPhones, an increase from the previous target of 7 to 8 million units, while stockpiling around 70 million iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units. All three models are expected to feature vapor chamber cooling technology.

As orders increase, reports indicate that Apple has resolved earlier hinge and yield issues, paving the way for higher production ahead of the September launch.
